reason: The cited evidence confirms the alloy can be made amorphous by melt-spinning (E2, E3) and reports crystallization temperatures for primary phases under slow cooling (E3), but it provides no data on sub-crystallization annealing, structural relaxation effects, or their impact on nucleation density and thermal stability. The key mechanistic premises are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Primary crystallization occurs above ~1000 K (e.g., FCC A at 1706 K, orthorhombic E at 1291 K under slow cooling)
Sub-crystallization annealing (900–1000 K) induces structural relaxation
Structural relaxation reduces nucleation sites for primary crystallization
Reduced nucleation sites increase crystallization onset temperature and amorphous retention
